headline: Bitcoin fell to a 12-week low after Nvidia's CEO resigned, US authorities moved to seize $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack, and Fed officials kept leaning toward another rate hike.

market.asOf: Read about 23:56-23:59 UTC Thu 12 Nov (06:56-06:59 Fri Bangkok; about 7pm ET). BTC and ETH from their CoinGecko pages; SOL from The Block's price page because CoinGecko's SOL page could not be opened. The Fear & Greed Index could not be read this run, so it is left out. Use the live prices on this page.

stories.title: Bitcoin stays near a 12-week low after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned
stories.summary: Nvidia said Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO and left its board, effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Bitcoin fell to its lowest level in nearly 12 weeks as Nvidia shares dropped, per The Block, while the major US stock averages were about flat, per CoinDesk.
points: Harvey Jones becomes board chair, and Q3 results are still set for 17 November, per CoinDesk.
Nvidia shares were down as much as about 14% during the day, per CoinDesk's live blog.
Bitcoin hit a low of $71,200, its lowest in nearly 12 weeks, per The Block.
In the 24 hours to 20:33 UTC, $284.49M of leveraged bitcoin bets were force-closed (liquidated), and about 95% of them were bets on rising prices, per CoinGlass.
President Trump said Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Huang; neither company has said Cook is being considered, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: US moves to seize $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack and shuts down a deepfake video-call scam
stories.summary: The Justice Department got court approval to seize or hold more than $1.2B of the crypto stolen from Binance in October, which the FBI blames on a North Korea-linked hacking group. The FBI also seized the servers behind "FaceStealer", a scam that used fake Zoom or Teams calls with recorded or deepfake video of people victims knew, then tricked them into installing wallet-draining software. This is progress on recovering the money, but it does not mean the funds have been returned yet. Earlier on Thursday, Binance said it had fully covered affected customers.
points: More than $1.2B is approved for seizure or restraint, part of more than $2.7B frozen so far by US authorities and private companies, per CoinDesk and The Block.
The total stolen is reported as more than $6B by CoinDesk and The Block and about $6.3B by The Record.
FaceStealer took more than $400M over about 18 months, per Decrypt.
Binance set aside $6.34B to cover the loss, per The Block.
Safety tip: never install a "fix" someone sends you during a video call, even if the caller looks like someone you know.

stories.title: Fed officials keep signalling more rate hikes
stories.summary: Several Federal Reserve officials leaned toward raising interest rates again on Thursday. Higher rates make safe savings pay more, which tends to pull money away from risky assets like crypto. Friday's producer-price report (a measure of inflation) at 8:30am ET is the next test.
points: Markets priced a 94% chance of a quarter-point hike at the 9 December meeting, per CoinDesk at 10:55am ET Thursday.
The 10-year Treasury yield was above 5% and gold was at $3,868, its lowest since September 2025, per CoinDesk.
Cleveland Fed President Hammack said inflation pressures are broadening but prefers smaller, steadier hikes, per CoinDesk.
San Francisco Fed President Daly expects further hikes but favours gradual tightening, per Newsquawk.

briefs.title: White House names SEC and CFTC nominees
briefs.summary: Four nominees were named, the first in about a year: Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine for the SEC, and Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland for the CFTC, which now has 1 of 5 seats filled, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Gemini's revenue falls 19%
briefs.summary: Crypto exchange Gemini (GEMI) reported Q3 revenue of $40.9M, down 19%, trading volume of $4.5B against $16.4B a year earlier, and a net loss of $58.6M; its call is Friday 8:30am ET, per the company release.

briefs.title: Louisiana sues 10 prediction-market platforms
briefs.summary: Louisiana sued Kalshi, Robinhood, Polymarket, Coinbase, Crypto.com, Gemini and four others, seeking a restraining order; it is the 11th state to sue, per The Block.

briefs.title: Bitcoin funds lose about $300M in a day
briefs.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $300M on Wednesday, including about $270M from BlackRock's IBIT, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: MSCI to drop Strategy
briefs.summary: Strategy (MSTR) will leave MSCI's indexes after the 30 November close, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Cisco beats and raises its forecast
briefs.summary: Cisco reported revenue of around $18.5B, up 24%, and raised its full-year outlook, citing AI demand from big cloud companies, per InvestingLive.

briefs.title: New York sets crypto advertising rules
briefs.summary: New York's financial regulator told crypto firms not to make misleading "no fee" claims and to disclose paid testimonials, with review processes due by 10 May 2027, per The Block.

briefs.title: US home sales hit lowest since 2010
briefs.summary: Existing home sales fell to 3.75M in October, the lowest since August 2010, per CoinDesk.
